title: Aishah, in the same room, missed her words. Allah heard them.
subtitle: Khawlah's plea, answered from above the heavens
then: Khawlah bint Tha'labah came to the Prophet ﷺ about her husband Aws. She said: {trap}he spent my wealth, used up my youth, and when I grew old he pronounced zihar on me.{/trap} Aishah, in the same room, could not hear all of it. She later said: {idea}Blessed is He whose hearing encompasses all things.{/idea}
now: You are in the hospital corridor whispering to Allah, or crying quietly in the car outside your house. No one around can hear you. {idea}The surah is named after a woman exactly like you,{/idea} whose quiet complaint got an answer.
old: My private struggles are too small for Allah to care about.
new: Allah heard a woman whispering her pain and answered her with Quran.
try: Tell Allah one complaint today, in your own words, like Khawlah did.

title: Calling your wife your mother does not make it true.
subtitle: An old custom named for what it is
then: Ibn Kathir explains that in the time before Islam, a man would say to his wife, {trap}to me you are like my mother's back{/trap}, and it worked as a divorce. The verse says plainly: your mothers are only those who gave birth to you. It is {trap}an ugly word and a lie{/trap}, yet {reward}Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.{/reward}
now: In a fight, you say the cruel thing. I wish I never married you. You are dead to me. You know it is not true, but you said it to wound. {idea}The verse calls that kind of sentence what it is.{/idea} And it leaves the door open to repair.
old: Words said in anger do not really count.
new: Words said in anger can be lies that wound. Allah sees them, and still pardons.
try: Think of one harsh thing you said in anger. Take it back today, out loud.

title: Taking back words has a cost.
subtitle: Why a careless sentence needs making up for
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah allowed this community to make expiation for zihar instead of it ending the marriage, as it did before Islam. The verse ends: {idea}that is an admonition to you, and Allah is Aware of what you do.{/idea} The cost teaches {trap}that a careless sentence is not nothing.{/trap}
now: You sent the angry voice note to your spouse at midnight. In the morning you want to act like it never happened. {idea}Real repair costs something{/idea}: an apology, a gesture, effort. Skipping that step is how words pile up.
old: If I regret what I said, we can just move on.
new: Words have weight. Repairing them means doing something, not just forgetting.
try: For one hurtful thing you said, do something kind for that person today.

title: When he could do none of it, help came in a basket.
subtitle: Mercy built into the limits of Allah

row.title: baskets of dates
sub: from the Prophet ﷺ and her

then: Khawlah reported that each option was named, and each time she said her husband could not. Then the Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}we will help him with a basket of dates.{/reward} She said: and I will help with another. He told her: {idea}you have done well. Give it on his behalf and take care of your cousin.{/idea}
now: Your spouse messed up and now has to make it right, but cannot manage it alone. You could stand back and watch. Khawlah, who had just been wronged, {reward}brought her own basket.{/reward} That is what the limits of Allah looked like up close.
old: If someone wronged me, fixing it is entirely their problem.
new: Sometimes the one who was hurt helps the other carry the repair.
try: Help someone today with a mistake they are trying to fix, even if it hurt you.

title: Clear signs came down. Opposing them leads to disgrace.
subtitle: What happens to those who defy the limits
then: Right after the limits about zihar, the surah warns. Maududi notes it is contrary to faith to {trap}persist in the practices of ignorance after accepting Islam{/trap}, or make rules that contradict Allah's. Ibn Kathir says this disgrace is just recompense for {trap}arrogant refusal to follow and submit.{/trap}
now: You know what the verse says. But your family has always done it differently, and changing feels awkward. {idea}The verses are clear. The question is whether you let them win over habit.{/idea}
old: Old customs are fine to keep, even when they clash with the Quran.
new: When the verses are clear, holding on to an old custom against them is defiance.
try: Name one habit you keep only because it is tradition. Check it against the Quran.

title: You forgot it. Allah kept count.
subtitle: The Day every deed is read back
then: Ibn Kathir explains that on the Day, Allah gathers the first and last generations and {idea}tells them all they did in detail, good or evil.{/idea} He recorded it all, {trap}even though they have forgotten.{/trap} Nothing escapes His knowledge or observation.
now: Scroll back five years in your messages. Things you said, promises you made, kindnesses you did, all forgotten. {idea}None of it was forgotten by Him.{/idea} That includes the good you no longer remember doing.
old: If I cannot even remember it, it does not matter anymore.
new: What I forget, Allah has counted, the good and the bad.
try: Before bed, review your day for two minutes and ask forgiveness for what you find.

title: Three people whispering? He is the fourth.
subtitle: No private conversation is truly private
then: Ibn Kathir explains that whether three or five people talk in secret, Allah is with them, {idea}hearing their speech, public or secret{/idea}, and His angels record it. Scholars agree this "with" refers to His knowledge. Imam Ahmad noted the verse {idea}begins and ends with His knowledge.{/idea}
now: The side chat with two coworkers about the new manager. The three of you on the balcony at the wedding, talking about the bride's family. {idea}Count again. There is always one more in the conversation.{/idea}
old: What I say in a private chat stays between us.
new: Every private conversation has Allah in it, hearing every word.
try: In your next private chat, say only what you would say with Allah listening.

title: A greeting twisted into a curse.
subtitle: Secret talk, a poisoned hello, and false safety
then: Some people in Madinah would greet the Prophet ﷺ with {trap}as-sam alayka{/trap}, death be upon you, instead of peace. Aishah answered with a curse. The Prophet ﷺ told her: {idea}Allah does not like rudeness and foul speech{/idea}, and said he had simply replied, and upon you. They thought no punishment meant no harm.
now: The coworker who says something passive-aggressive dressed up as a joke. You have the perfect cutting reply ready. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ answered a curse with two calm words.{/idea} And when you get away with something, do not read silence as approval.
old: If someone insults me, I am justified in being as rude as they were.
new: I can answer rudeness calmly. And Allah's delay is not His approval.
try: The next time someone is rude to you today, answer in as few, calm words as you can.

title: Whisper, but whisper about good.
subtitle: Private talk for righteousness, not harm

row.title: private, still for good
sub: you will be gathered to Him

then: After the bad example, believers get the alternative. Ibn Kathir notes that {trap}sin harms yourself, aggression harms others.{/trap} Instead, {reward}speak privately about righteousness and taqwa{/reward}, remembering you will be gathered to Allah, who has counted every word.
now: The family group chat without your sister-in-law in it. It could be for gossip. Or it could be where you secretly plan her surprise birthday, or quietly pool money for a relative in debt. {reward}Same chat, different purpose.{/reward}
old: Private conversations are where we finally say what we really think about people.
new: Private conversations can be where good things are quietly planned.
try: Use one private message today to plan something kind for someone.

title: Evil whispers aim to sadden you, but cannot harm without permission.
subtitle: When you see people whispering about you
then: Ibn Kathir says the companions would sometimes see people whispering and {trap}fear they were being plotted against{/trap}, even changing their route. The verse says this kind of talk is from Shaytan, to grieve believers. {idea}It cannot harm them except as Allah permits{/idea}, so seek refuge and trust Him.
now: You walk into the staff room and two people stop talking and look at you. Your mind races for the rest of the day. {idea}That anxiety is the whole point of the whisper.{/idea} Put it in Allah's hands, and refuse to carry it home.
old: If people whisper when I walk in, something bad is coming for me.
new: Whispers are meant to unsettle me, but nothing reaches me without Allah's permission.
try: Next time you feel talked about, say hasbiyallah and move on with your task.

title: Make room for others, and Allah makes room for you.
subtitle: Manners of the gathering, and who is raised
then: Qatadah said people in gatherings with the Prophet ﷺ {trap}would hesitate to make room for newcomers so they would not lose their places.{/trap} The verse told them to spread out. Ibn Kathir notes the reward matches the deed, and says {reward}whoever humbles himself, Allah elevates.{/reward}
now: The packed mosque on Eid. Someone squeezes in at the end of your row and you could shuffle over, or stay put with your elbows out. {reward}Shift over. Allah widens things for you{/reward}, in ways you will not see coming.
old: If I give up my spot, I lose something.
new: Making room for others is how Allah makes room and raises me.
try: Today, give your seat, spot, or turn to someone else without being asked.

title: Give something before taking the Prophet's ﷺ time.
subtitle: A short-lived command about private meetings

row.title: his time is free
sub: I can take all I want

then: Ibn Abbas said the Muslims {trap}kept asking the Prophet ﷺ questions until it became difficult on him.{/trap} Allah lightened his burden with this verse: give charity before a private meeting. Those who could not afford it were excused, since {reward}Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.{/reward} Ali said he was the only one who acted on it before it was lifted.
now: You message your busy friend who is a doctor, a lawyer, an imam, with your fifth question this week. Free advice feels free. {idea}But their time is not free.{/idea} The verse taught people to value someone's time before taking it.
old: If someone is generous with their time, I can take as much as I like.
new: Other people's time is precious. I should honour it before I ask for it.
try: Before asking someone for help today, offer them something first, even just thanks.

title: The extra was lifted. The basics remain.
subtitle: Allah eased the command and pointed back to prayer
then: Ibn Abbas said many {trap}were afraid to pay this charity and stopped asking.{/trap} Then this verse came: since you did not, and Allah has forgiven you, {idea}establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger.{/idea} Qatadah said the earlier command lasted only about an hour of a day. {reward}Allah made things easy for them.{/reward}
now: Your ambitious plan of extra worship fell apart this week. You feel like a failure. The verse does not scold. {idea}It says: fine, keep the foundations.{/idea} Your five prayers today still count fully.
old: If I could not do the extra, I have failed completely.
new: When the extra is too much, Allah eases it. The basics are still the heart.
try: Whatever else slipped this week, pray your next prayer on time and with care.

title: Neither with you nor with them.
subtitle: The hypocrites who played both sides

row.title: the believers
sub: we are with you, they swore

row.title: belong nowhere
sub: neither of you nor of them

then: Ibn Kathir explains that the hypocrites in Madinah {trap}secretly aided the Muslims' opponents{/trap}, while swearing to the Prophet ﷺ that they were believers. They knew they were lying. The verse says they are {trap}neither of you nor of them{/trap}, swaying between the two, as another verse describes.
now: At work you agree with whoever is in the room. With one team you mock the other, then you do the reverse. Everyone thinks you are on their side. {idea}In the end, no one trusts you, including yourself.{/idea}
old: If I tell each side what they want to hear, I stay safe with everyone.
new: Playing both sides leaves me belonging to no one.
try: Today, say what you actually think in one conversation, kindly and honestly.

title: What they were doing was evil, and it has a cost.
subtitle: Deceit and betrayal are not small
then: Ibn Kathir explains the punishment is {trap}on account of their evil deeds{/trap}: their support of the opponents, {trap}and their deceit and betrayal of the believers.{/trap} The verse states it simply: evil is what they used to do.
now: Leaking a friend's secret to get in with another group. Forwarding a colleague's private message to the boss. It feels like strategy. {idea}The verse calls betrayal by its real name.{/idea} And there is still time to stop.
old: A bit of double-dealing is just how life works.
new: Betraying people who trust me is an evil deed, not a clever move.
try: If you are holding someone's secret, guard it today as a trust.

title: They used oaths as a shield.
subtitle: Swearing by Allah to hide the truth
then: Ibn Kathir says the hypocrites {trap}concealed disbelief under the shield of their false oaths.{/trap} Many people were fooled and so were turned from Allah's path. The humiliation is recompense for {idea}belittling the significance of swearing by the Mighty Name of Allah.{/idea}
now: Wallahi I sent it already. Wallahi I am on my way. Said while still at home on the sofa. {idea}Allah's name is not filler{/idea} to make an excuse sound true.
old: Swearing by Allah is just a way to make people believe me.
new: Allah's name is too great to be used as cover for a lie.
try: Today, do not swear by Allah at all unless it is completely true and needed.

title: Wealth and children cannot shield anyone from Allah.
subtitle: What the hypocrites relied on
then: Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}none of their possessions can avert the affliction{/trap} when it comes. The hypocrites' false oaths protected them among people, and their wealth and sons gave them standing. {idea}None of it works before Allah.{/idea}
now: The family name that opens doors. The savings that make you feel untouchable. The sons who would defend you in any argument. {idea}Good things, but not shields{/idea} when you stand before Allah.
old: With enough money and family behind me, I am protected.
new: Only what I truly believed and did protects me before Allah.
try: Thank Allah for your family and wealth today, and remind yourself they are gifts, not shields.

title: They will try to lie to Allah too.
subtitle: How you live is how you are raised

row.title: I can change at the end

then: Ibn Kathir says they will swear to Allah they were guided, {trap}just as they used to swear to the believers.{/trap} He adds: {idea}those who live on a certain path will most likely die on it, and be resurrected on it.{/idea} The verse answers: they are the liars.
now: Small lies at work, at home, to the delivery driver. It becomes reflex. The verse shows where a reflex leads: {trap}lying even when it is useless.{/trap} {idea}The habits you build now are the ones you will carry.{/idea}
old: Small lies are harmless. I can always be honest when it really matters.
new: What I practise now becomes who I am, even on the Day I meet Allah.
try: Catch one small, reflexive lie today and replace it with the truth.

title: Shaytan wins by making you forget Allah.
subtitle: Forgetting remembrance is the first loss
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Shaytan {trap}took over their hearts until he made them forget Allah.{/trap} He cites the hadith: any three in a village or desert who do not establish prayer among them, Shaytan takes control of them, {idea}so stay with the congregation, for the wolf eats the strayed sheep.{/idea}
now: You used to go to the mosque with friends. Then work got busy, then you prayed at home, then you started missing prayers. {trap}No big decision, just drifting.{/trap} {idea}The way back is often other people praying with you.{/idea}
old: I can keep my faith strong on my own, without anyone.
new: Forgetting Allah happens slowly, and staying close to others who pray protects me.
try: Pray one prayer with someone today, at home or at the mosque.

title: Those who oppose Allah end among the most humbled.
subtitle: Defiance looks strong, then it falls
then: Ibn Kathir explains that those who stubbornly defy Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, and stay away from the truth, are {trap}among the miserable, banished from goodness{/trap}, humbled in this life and the next. {idea}Guidance is in one place, defiance in another.{/idea}
now: The moment you know you are wrong but dig in anyway, because backing down feels weak. With your parents, your spouse, with a clear verse. {idea}Digging in against the truth only lowers you.{/idea}
old: Never backing down makes me strong.
new: Standing against the truth always ends in being brought low.
try: Admit you were wrong about one thing today, to Allah or to a person.

title: It is already written: Allah and His messengers prevail.
subtitle: The ending is decided
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}decreed in the First Book, in a way that can never be changed, that final victory belongs to Him, His messengers and the believers{/idea}, in this life and the next. He cites another verse: {reward}the good end is for those who have taqwa.{/reward}
now: You are the only one in your office who will not fudge the numbers. It costs you. Sometimes it feels like honest people always lose. {idea}This verse is the last page of the story, already written.{/idea}
old: Doing right looks like a losing game.
new: The outcome is already written, and it belongs to Allah and those with Him.
try: Hold on to one right choice today that feels costly, and trust the ending.

title: Pleased with Allah, and Allah pleased with them.
subtitle: When love for Allah comes before every tie
then: Ibn Kathir reports this verse was said to concern companions at Badr who stood against their own relatives who opposed Allah. He notes {idea}a beautiful secret{/idea}: when they let go of those ties for Allah's sake, {reward}He compensated them by being pleased with them, and making them pleased with Him.{/reward}
now: Your family pushes you toward something you know is wrong: a dishonest deal, a cruel decision, missing prayer for a party. Saying no feels like betrayal. {idea}This verse says Allah's pleasure is worth that cost,{/idea} and He fills the gap.
old: Keeping my family happy matters more than anything else.
new: When love for anyone pulls me from Allah, His pleasure comes first, and He makes up for it.
try: Make dua for a relative you disagree with about faith, that Allah guides you both.
